decision: THRESHOLD-FALSIFIED-BUT-SEPARATION-CONFIRMED. Triggered by drafting 5.6: the skeleton derived 'mask-free RPE > 2.5 cm/frame => the mask becomes necessary' from exactly TWO sequences (pt2 1.572 redundant, pt1 2.894 necessary) and defended it as 'not arbitrary, it comes from a controlled pair of same-type sequences'. But a threshold placed between the only two points that define it is fitted, not tested -- with n=2 every value in (1.57, 2.89) separates them equally. Registered the necessity readout BEFORE looking: N = ATE(mask-free)/ATE(combined), N>=1.5 necessary, N<=1.2 redundant, 1.2<N<1.5 ambiguous and EXCLUDED rather than forced to a side. Provenance: seeds and per-cell ATE read through the main-table builder's own discover()/read_ate(), RPE by the same per-run-CSV-first order, so this check cannot diverge from the table's latest-run rule. RESULT A -- the 2.5 threshold is FALSIFIED: 13/17 decided cells agree (76%), and the 4 misclassifications are severe, all in the direction of underestimating mask necessity: f3_wk_xyz RPE 1.717 but N=8.76x, f3_wk_hf 2.327 but N=5.27x, balloon 2.028 but N=3.96x, f3_wk_rpy 2.264 but N=3.41x. The value 2.5 sits ABOVE the real boundary precisely because pt2 (1.572) and pt1 (2.894) bracket a wide empty gap, so interpolating between them skips the whole 1.7-2.4 band where the mask is necessary without RPE being high. RESULT B -- the underlying rule is nevertheless CONFIRMED, and more strongly than claimed: mask-free RPE separates the two groups with NO OVERLAP -- redundant group 0.222-1.572 (f2_xyz, f3_office, f2_person, f1_desk, f3_st_xyz, mv_no_box, f3_st_rpy, mv_no_box2, pt2) vs necessary group 1.717-2.980 (f3_wk_xyz, balloon, f3_wk_rpy, f3_wk_hf, crowd, balloon2, pt1, crowd2) -- so ANY threshold in (1.572, 1.717) separates all 17 decided cells, midpoint ~1.64 cm/frame. The one excluded cell does not prop the rule up: f3_st_hf (N=1.21, RPE 1.041) would AGREE if counted, giving 18/18. NOT A TAUTOLOGY: f3_st_hf and crowd have nearly identical mask-free ATE (35.59 vs 34.89) but N differing 12.6x (1.21 vs 15.24), and mask-free RPE is what separates them (1.041 vs 2.643) -- per-frame drift predicts whether the mask will help where full-trajectory ATE does not, which is directionally consistent with exp37's ENDPOINT-DECOUPLED finding. SCOPE (all must travel with the claim): the (1.572, 1.717) interval is FITTED to the same 18 sequences that define it, with NO held-out set, so it is descriptive and must be pre-registered and tested on new sequences before being called a criterion; and computing mask-free RPE requires RUNNING the mask-free arm, so it is a post-hoc DIAGNOSTIC, not a deployable a-priori selector. It does however satisfy the roadmap's hard requirement that a regime selector come from a MASK-FREE observable (unlike the already-falsified sequence-level semantic-area candidate, which needed a semantic detector), so future work moves from 'no candidate exists' to 'one candidate measured, needs prereg + new sequences'. ACTIONS: skeleton.md 3.1 annotated in place retracting both the 2.5 value and its 'not arbitrary' defence (data untouched); 3 forbidden phrasings added to WRITING_ROADMAP 6; the future-work wording upgraded. SEPARATE IN-PLACE RETRACTION, same session: bracketing_pt1_pt2_scene.md 2's 'dynamic pixels = 64.7% mean / 86-90% max' is not reproducible -- wphs_person_area_characterization.md measured pt1 person area at mean 7.31% / median 11.11% / max 20.24% over all 580 frames and had already recorded that the '~65% of frame' figure fails under the mask-ON protocol -- and that file's statistics scripts were never committed (self-described as living in /tmp), so its 2/3/4 are unreproducible under the exp43 provenance gate; its 3's '11-12 m person-camera distance' is implausible for indoor BONN, corroborating a measurement fault rather than a recall difference. Built the v1 body for real -- wrote scripts/md2latex_manuscript.py (a converter scoped to exactly the constructs this manuscript uses: ATX headings, bold/italic, inline code, inline and display math, pipe tables, blockquote figure captions, lists) plus latex/main_v1.tex as a measurement driver, and compiled with tectonic under llncs.cls. CALIBRATION METHOD: deliberately used FOUR document lengths rather than two, because two points fit any line exactly -- the same trap as criterion #26 from this session's RPE work. Least squares over (2011,6),(3397,9),(4859,12),(6503,16) gives 452.1 visible-LaTeX-words/page with a 1.48-page fixed overhead, residuals within +/-0.22 pages, and pairwise marginal rates 462/487/411 whose spread is page-break quantisation rather than model error. Converted to this project's markdown-word unit: ~477 words/page. TWO ERRORS IN THE OLD ACCOUNT, in opposite directions but not cancelling: the rate was 520 (9% optimistic, worth -0.6 page) and front matter was allowed 0.50 page against a measured 1.48 (worth +1.0 page), so the old model underestimated v1 by ~0.65 page before even counting the two figures that are referenced but not yet in the markdown (+0.65). CONSEQUENCE: v2 must cut ~5.5 pages, not the 4.35 recorded after the v1 pass. The v0->v1 compression itself was NOT wasted -- v0 is 18.4 pages at the measured rate against v1's 17.0, a real -3.3. TWO STRATEGY CORRECTIONS the measurement produced: (a) table merging is NOT the lever it was assumed to be -- 5 footnotesize booktabs tables plus a figure placeholder cost 1.0 page total against the 2.0 the old account reserved for 7 floats, so the remaining cuts must come from prose and front matter; (b) the abstract is expensive -- title block + 200-word abstract + keywords is 1.48 pages, so writing to the 200-word ceiling is a real page decision. SCOPE: no bibliography in the build (LNCS puts references outside the 12-page body, so this does not affect the verdict, but it would if a venue counted them); Fig2/Fig3 are referenced by the body yet absent from the markdown, so 17.6 is EXTRAPOLATED not measured, and all three figures should be in the build before the final decision; the converter is document-specific and its table/figure styling choices set every number here; page-break quantisation gives ~+/-8% (+/-1.2 pages at 17), so 17 must be read as 17 +/- 1 and not used for half-page decisions; and the four calibration points are prefixes of one document rather than four independent documents, so a section whose float or equation density differs markedly from the whole will deviate from the fitted rate. ACTIONS: scripts/count_manuscript_pages.py recalibrated (RATE 520->477, FRONT_MATTER 0.50->1.48, plus an explicit MISSING_FIGURE_PAGES term and a +/-1 caveat in its own output); WRITING_ROADMAP 4-A rewritten with the measured constants and the two strategy corrections; the manuscript v1 footer and the frozen v0 header both restated in measured rather than estimated terms.
